Juniorer kan börja ro från 12 års ålder.

Säsongen börjar i april, när isen har gått.

### Kan jag prova innan jag går med?

Ja, vi har prova-på-kvällar varje tisdag i maj.

### Vad ska jag ha på mig?

Åtsittande träningskläder som du kan röra dig i.

### Får jag en nyckel till båthuset?

Ja, depositionen för nyckeln är 100 kr.

Gäster får ro två gånger per säsong tillsammans med en medlem.

Ja, gymmet är öppet året runt.

Båtarna är bara för medlemmar och kan inte hyras.

Boka i appen minst en timme i förväg.

### Finns det duschar?

Ja, det finns duschar och bastu i klubbhuset.

Privata båtar kan förvaras mot en avgift om det finns plats.

### Finns det skåp?

Ja, ett skåp kostar 100 kr per säsong.

Parkeringen bakom båthuset är gratis.

Ja, vi har en vårfest och en höstmiddag.

Mejla kassören före den 1 december.

Du kan pausa en säsong i taget.

En styrelse som väljs på årsmötet i mars.

Anmäl dig till en arbetsdag i klubbkalendern.

## Current en content:
# Frequently asked questions

### How do I become a member?

Fill in the form on the membership page.

### Do I need to know how to swim?

Yes, all members must be able to swim 200 metres.

### Is there an age limit?

Juniors can start rowing from the age of 12.

### When does the season start?

The season starts in April, when the ice has gone.

### Can I try before joining?

Yes, we hold try-out evenings every Tuesday in May.

### What should I wear?

Tight-fitting sports clothes that you can move in.

### Do I get a key to the boathouse?

Yes, the key deposit is 100 SEK.

### Can I bring a guest?

Guests may row twice per season with a member.

### Is coaching included?

Coaching on Tuesdays and Thursdays is included in the fee.

### Can I row alone?

Only after passing the sculling test.

### What happens in bad weather?

The duty officer decides whether boats may go out.

### Do you race?

We enter three regattas each summer.

### Is there a gym?

Yes, the gym is open all year round.

### Can I rent a boat?

Boats are for members only and cannot be rented.

### How do I book a boat?

Book in the app at least one hour ahead.

### Are there showers?

Yes, there are showers and a sauna in the clubhouse.

### Can I store my own boat?

Private boats can be stored for a fee if there is room.

### Do you have lockers?

Yes, lockers cost 150 SEK per season.

### Is there parking?

Parking is free behind the boathouse.

### Do you organise social events?

Yes, we hold a spring party and an autumn dinner.

### How do I cancel my membership?

Email the treasurer before 1 December.

### Can I pause my membership?

You can pause for one season at a time.

### Who runs the club?

A board elected at the annual meeting in March.

### How can I help out?

Sign up for a work day on the club calendar.

Juniors can start rowing from the age of 12.

Tight-fitting sports clothes that you can move in.

Only after passing the sculling test.

The duty officer decides whether boats may go out.

We enter three regattas each summer.

Boats are for members only and cannot be rented.

Book in the app at least one hour ahead.

Private boats can be stored for a fee if there is room.

Parking is free behind the boathouse.

Yes, we hold a spring party and an autumn dinner.

Email the treasurer before 1 December.

You can pause for one season at a time.

A board elected at the annual meeting in March.

Sign up for a work day on the club calendar.

## Current en content:
# Frequently asked questions

### How do I become a member?

Fill in the form on the membership page.

### Do I need to know how to swim?

Yes, all members must be able to swim 300 metres.

### Is there an age limit?

Juniors can start rowing from the age of 12.

### When does the season start?

The season starts in April, when the ice has gone.

### Can I try before joining?

Yes, we hold try-out evenings every Tuesday in May.

### What should I wear?

Tight-fitting sports clothes that you can move in.

### Do I get a key to the boathouse?

Yes, the key deposit is 100 SEK.

### Can I bring a guest?

Guests may row twice per season with a member.

### Is coaching included?

Coaching on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays is included in the fee.

### Can I row alone?

Only after passing the sculling test.

### What happens in bad weather?

The duty officer decides whether boats may go out.

### Do you race?

We enter three regattas each summer.

### Is there a gym?

Yes, the gym is open all year round.

### Can I rent a boat?

Boats are for members only and cannot be rented.

### How do I book a boat?

Book in the app at least two hours ahead.

### Are there showers?

Yes, there are showers and a sauna in the clubhouse.

### Can I store my own boat?

Private boats can be stored for a fee if there is room.

### Do you have lockers?

Yes, lockers cost 100 SEK per season.

### Is there parking?

Parking is free behind the boathouse.

### Do you organise social events?

Yes, we hold a spring party and an autumn dinner.

### How do I cancel my membership?

Email the treasurer before 1 December.

### Can I pause my membership?

You can pause for one season at a time.

### Who runs the club?

A board elected at the annual meeting in February.

### How can I help out?

Sign up for a work day on the club calendar.

You are keeping the Swedish (sv) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (English (en)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. # Vanliga frågor

### Hur blir jag medlem?

Fyll i formuläret på medlemssidan.

### Behöver jag kunna simma?

Ja, alla medlemmar måste kunna simma 200 meter.

### Finns det en åldersgräns?

Juniorer kan börja ro från 12 års ålder.

### När börjar säsongen?

Säsongen börjar i april, när isen har gått.

### Kan jag prova innan jag går med?

Ja, vi har prova-på-kvällar varje tisdag i maj.

### Vad ska jag ha på mig?

Åtsittande träningskläder som du kan röra dig i.

### Får jag en nyckel till båthuset?

Ja, depositionen för nyckeln är 100 kr.

### Får jag ta med en gäst?

Gäster får ro två gånger per säsong tillsammans med en medlem.

### Ingår träning med tränare?

Träning med tränare på tisdagar och torsdagar ingår i avgiften.

### Får jag ro ensam?

Först när du har klarat singelprovet.

### Vad händer vid dåligt väder?

Dagens ansvarige bestämmer om båtarna får gå ut.

### Tävlar ni?

Vi deltar i tre regattor varje sommar.

### Finns det ett gym?

Ja, gymmet är öppet året runt.

### Kan jag hyra en båt?

Båtarna är bara för medlemmar och kan inte hyras.

### Hur bokar jag en båt?

Boka i appen minst en timme i förväg.

### Finns det duschar?

Ja, det finns duschar och bastu i klubbhuset.

### Kan jag förvara min egen båt?

Privata båtar kan förvaras mot en avgift om det finns plats.

### Finns det skåp?

Ja, ett skåp kostar 100 kr per säsong.

### Finns det parkering?

Parkeringen bakom båthuset är gratis.

### Ordnar ni sociala aktiviteter?

Ja, vi har en vårfest och en höstmiddag.

### Hur säger jag upp mitt medlemskap?

Mejla kassören före den 1 december.

### Kan jag pausa mitt medlemskap?

Du kan pausa en säsong i taget.

### Vem driver klubben?

En styrelse som väljs på årsmötet i mars.

### Hur kan jag hjälpa till?

Anmäl dig till en arbetsdag i klubbkalendern.

# Vanliga frågor

### Hur blir jag medlem?

Fyll i formuläret på medlemssidan.

### Behöver jag kunna simma?

Ja, alla medlemmar måste kunna simma 200 meter.

### Finns det en åldersgräns?

Juniorer kan börja ro från 12 års ålder.

### När börjar säsongen?

Säsongen börjar i april, när isen har gått.

### Kan jag prova innan jag går med?

Ja, vi har prova-på-kvällar varje tisdag i maj.

### Vad ska jag ha på mig?

Åtsittande träningskläder som du kan röra dig i.

### Får jag en nyckel till båthuset?

Ja, depositionen för nyckeln är 100 kr.

### Får jag ta med en gäst?

Gäster får ro två gånger per säsong tillsammans med en medlem.

### Ingår träning med tränare?

Träning med tränare på tisdagar och torsdagar ingår i avgiften.

### Får jag ro ensam?

Först när du har klarat singelprovet.

### Vad händer vid dåligt väder?

Dagens ansvarige bestämmer om båtarna får gå ut.

### Tävlar ni?

Vi deltar i tre regattor varje sommar.

### Finns det ett gym?

Ja, gymmet är öppet året runt.

### Kan jag hyra en båt?

Båtarna är bara för medlemmar och kan inte hyras.

### Hur bokar jag en båt?

Boka i appen minst en timme i förväg.

### Finns det duschar?

Ja, det finns duschar och bastu i klubbhuset.

### Kan jag förvara min egen båt?

Privata båtar kan förvaras mot en avgift om det finns plats.

### Finns det skåp?

Ja, ett skåp kostar 100 kr per säsong.

### Finns det parkering?

Parkeringen bakom båthuset är gratis.

### Ordnar ni sociala aktiviteter?

Ja, vi har en vårfest och en höstmiddag.

### Hur säger jag upp mitt medlemskap?

Mejla kassören före den 1 december.

### Kan jag pausa mitt medlemskap?

Du kan pausa en säsong i taget.

### Vem driver klubben?

En styrelse som väljs på årsmötet i mars.

### Hur kan jag hjälpa till?

Anmäl dig till en arbetsdag i klubbkalendern.

# Frequently asked questions

### How do I become a member?

Fill in the form on the membership page.

### Do I need to know how to swim?

Yes, all members must be able to swim 200 metres.

### Is there an age limit?

Juniors can start rowing from the age of 12.

### When does the season start?

The season starts in April, when the ice has gone.

### Can I try before joining?

Yes, we hold try-out evenings every Tuesday in May.

### What should I wear?

Tight-fitting sports clothes that you can move in.

### Do I get a key to the boathouse?

Yes, the key deposit is 100 SEK.

### Can I bring a guest?

Guests may row twice per season with a member.

### Is coaching included?

Coaching on Tuesdays and Thursdays is included in the fee.

### Can I row alone?

Only after passing the sculling test.

### What happens in bad weather?

The duty officer decides whether boats may go out.

### Do you race?

We enter three regattas each summer.

### Is there a gym?

Yes, the gym is open all year round.

### Can I rent a boat?

Boats are for members only and cannot be rented.

### How do I book a boat?

Book in the app at least one hour ahead.

### Are there showers?

Yes, there are showers and a sauna in the clubhouse.

### Can I store my own boat?

Private boats can be stored for a fee if there is room.

### Do you have lockers?

Yes, lockers cost 150 SEK per season.

### Is there parking?

Parking is free behind the boathouse.

### Do you organise social events?

Yes, we hold a spring party and an autumn dinner.

### How do I cancel my membership?

Email the treasurer before 1 December.

### Can I pause my membership?

You can pause for one season at a time.

### Who runs the club?

A board elected at the annual meeting in March.

### How can I help out?

Sign up for a work day on the club calendar.

### Hur blir jag medlem?

Fyll i formuläret på medlemssidan.

### Behöver jag kunna simma?

Ja, alla medlemmar måste kunna simma 200 meter.

### Finns det en åldersgräns?

Juniorer kan börja ro från 12 års ålder.

### När börjar säsongen?

Säsongen börjar i april, när isen har gått.

### Kan jag prova innan jag går med?

Ja, vi har prova-på-kvällar varje tisdag i maj.

### Vad ska jag ha på mig?

Åtsittande träningskläder som du kan röra dig i.

### Får jag en nyckel till båthuset?

Ja, depositionen för nyckeln är 100 kr.

### Får jag ta med en gäst?

Gäster får ro två gånger per säsong tillsammans med en medlem.

### Ingår träning med tränare?

Träning med tränare på tisdagar och torsdagar ingår i avgiften.

### Får jag ro ensam?

Först när du har klarat singelprovet.

### Vad händer vid dåligt väder?

Dagens ansvarige bestämmer om båtarna får gå ut.

### Tävlar ni?

Vi deltar i tre regattor varje sommar.

### Finns det ett gym?

Ja, gymmet är öppet året runt.

### Kan jag hyra en båt?

Båtarna är bara för medlemmar och kan inte hyras.

### Hur bokar jag en båt?

Boka i appen minst en timme i förväg.

### Finns det duschar?

Ja, det finns duschar och bastu i klubbhuset.

### Kan jag förvara min egen båt?

Privata båtar kan förvaras mot en avgift om det finns plats.

### Finns det skåp?

Ja, ett skåp kostar 100 kr per säsong.

### Finns det parkering?

Parkeringen bakom båthuset är gratis.

### Ordnar ni sociala aktiviteter?

Ja, vi har en vårfest och en höstmiddag.

### Hur säger jag upp mitt medlemskap?

Mejla kassören före den 1 december.

### Kan jag pausa mitt medlemskap?

Du kan pausa en säsong i taget.

### Vem driver klubben?

En styrelse som väljs på årsmötet i mars.

### Hur kan jag hjälpa till?

Anmäl dig till en arbetsdag i klubbkalendern.

# Frequently asked questions

### How do I become a member?

Fill in the form on the membership page.

### Do I need to know how to swim?

Yes, all members must be able to swim 200 metres.

### Is there an age limit?

Juniors can start rowing from the age of 12.

### When does the season start?

The season starts in April, when the ice has gone.

### Can I try before joining?

Yes, we hold try-out evenings every Tuesday in May.

### What should I wear?

Tight-fitting sports clothes that you can move in.

### Do I get a key to the boathouse?

Yes, the key deposit is 100 SEK.

### Can I bring a guest?

Guests may row twice per season with a member.

### Is coaching included?

Coaching on Tuesdays and Thursdays is included in the fee.

### Can I row alone?

Only after passing the sculling test.

### What happens in bad weather?

The duty officer decides whether boats may go out.

### Do you race?

We enter three regattas each summer.

### Is there a gym?

Yes, the gym is open all year round.

### Can I rent a boat?

Boats are for members only and cannot be rented.

### How do I book a boat?

Book in the app at least one hour ahead.

### Are there showers?

Yes, there are showers and a sauna in the clubhouse.

### Can I store my own boat?

Private boats can be stored for a fee if there is room.

### Do you have lockers?

Yes, lockers cost 150 SEK per season.

### Is there parking?

Parking is free behind the boathouse.

### Do you organise social events?

Yes, we hold a spring party and an autumn dinner.

### How do I cancel my membership?

Email the treasurer before 1 December.

### Can I pause my membership?

You can pause for one season at a time.

### Who runs the club?

A board elected at the annual meeting in March.

### How can I help out?

Sign up for a work day on the club calendar.

### Hur blir jag medlem?

Fyll i formuläret på medlemssidan.

### Behöver jag kunna simma?

Ja, alla medlemmar måste kunna simma 200 meter.

### Finns det en åldersgräns?

Juniorer kan börja ro från 12 års ålder.

### När börjar säsongen?

Säsongen börjar i april, när isen har gått.

### Kan jag prova innan jag går med?

Ja, vi har prova-på-kvällar varje tisdag i maj.

### Vad ska jag ha på mig?

Åtsittande träningskläder som du kan röra dig i.

### Får jag en nyckel till båthuset?

Ja, depositionen för nyckeln är 100 kr.

### Får jag ta med en gäst?

Gäster får ro två gånger per säsong tillsammans med en medlem.

### Ingår träning med tränare?

Träning med tränare på tisdagar och torsdagar ingår i avgiften.

### Får jag ro ensam?

Först när du har klarat singelprovet.

### Vad händer vid dåligt väder?

Dagens ansvarige bestämmer om båtarna får gå ut.

### Tävlar ni?

Vi deltar i tre regattor varje sommar.

### Finns det ett gym?

Ja, gymmet är öppet året runt.

### Kan jag hyra en båt?

Båtarna är bara för medlemmar och kan inte hyras.

Boka i appen minst en timme i förväg.

### Finns det duschar?

Ja, det finns duschar och bastu i klubbhuset.

### Kan jag förvara min egen båt?

Privata båtar kan förvaras mot en avgift om det finns plats.

### Finns det skåp?

Ja, ett skåp kostar 100 kr per säsong.

### Finns det parkering?

Parkeringen bakom båthuset är gratis.

### Ordnar ni sociala aktiviteter?

Ja, vi har en vårfest och en höstmiddag.

### Hur säger jag upp mitt medlemskap?

Mejla kassören före den 1 december.

### Kan jag pausa mitt medlemskap?

Du kan pausa en säsong i taget.

### Vem driver klubben?

En styrelse som väljs på årsmötet i mars.

### Hur kan jag hjälpa till?

Anmäl dig till en arbetsdag i klubbkalendern.

One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

You are keeping the Swedish (sv) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (English (en)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

You are keeping the Swedish (sv) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (English (en)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Markup is not text. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:

- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. You are keeping the English (en) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (Swedish (sv)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since English was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current English page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the English page up to date with the current Swedish page: find what it says that English does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the English page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in English: everywhere English states it, so that English does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when English says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder English.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for English. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose English pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in English follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is English, written as a English writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the English page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in English or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the English file. Each edit's result shows the English file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the English file, fix it with further edits. When the English file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

You are keeping the English (en) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (Swedish (sv)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since English was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current English page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the English page up to date with the current Swedish page: find what it says that English does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the English page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in English: everywhere English states it, so that English does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when English says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder English.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for English. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose English pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in English follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is English, written as a English writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the English page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in English or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the English file. Each edit's result shows the English file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the English file, fix it with further edits. When the English file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

You are keeping the English (en) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (Swedish (sv)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since English was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current English page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the English page up to date with the current Swedish page: find what it says that English does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the English page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in English: everywhere English states it, so that English does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when English says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder English.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for English. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose English pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in English follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is English, written as a English writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the English page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in English or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the English file. Each edit's result shows the English file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the English file, fix it with further edits. When the English file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

You are keeping the English (en) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (Swedish (sv)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since English was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current English page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the English page up to date with the current Swedish page: find what it says that English does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the English page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in English: everywhere English states it, so that English does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when English says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder English.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for English. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose English pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in English follow that convention too. One or more of them may have changed since English was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current English page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the English page up to date with the current Swedish page: find what it says that English does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the English page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in English: everywhere English states it, so that English does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when English says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder English.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for English. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose English pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in English follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is English, written as a English writer would put it, not word for word.

Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the English file, fix it with further edits. When the English file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. You are keeping the Swedish (sv) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (English (en)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

You are keeping the Swedish (sv) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (English (en)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

You are keeping the Swedish (sv) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (English (en)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

You are keeping the Swedish (sv) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (English (en)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Markup is not text. You are keeping the Swedish (sv) version of a document up to date with its other language versions (English (en)). The languages are equal peers; none is the original. One or more of them may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

  title="Acme"
  subtitle="Acme is the world's best tournament system for the world's best tournaments"
  ctaText="Learn more about Acme"
  ctaLink="/en/missa-inte/"
  backgroundMedia="/media/start-video-002-optimized.mp4"
  poster="/media/home/hero-poster.jpg"
/>

<CmSection id="sect-e5f6a7b8"
  heading="What is Acme?"
  contain="true"
  align="left"
  body={"Acme helps you as a tournament organiser deliver a smooth, fantastic overall experience to your participants. From registration, payment, draws and match schedules to live reporting of goals and final results on the web, in mobile apps or via SMS.\n\nWe've made it simple for tournaments of every size and complexity, big or small."}
  divider={true}
  contained={true}
/>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-2c8d91e4"
  eyebrow="Smarter scheduling with AI"
  title="How it works in Acme"
  ctaText="Read more about AI in Acme here"
  ctaLink="/en/vara-ai-losningar/"
  image="/media/home/ai-image-copy-1.webp"
  imageAlt="AI scheduling in Acme"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>
  Building a match schedule that actually works is a complex puzzle – especially with hundreds or thousands of matches, multiple venues, rest periods and special requests to consider.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-7f04b3a9"
  eyebrow="CASE STUDY: FJORDBY BASKET FESTIVAL"
  title="One of our customers shares their story"
  ctaText="Read about Fjordby Basket Festival here"
  ctaLink="/en/fjordby-basket-festival/"
  image="/media/home/customer-story.png"
  imageAlt="Fjordby Basket Festival"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>

</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-91d5c0e7"
  eyebrow="WE'RE PROUD OF OUR SUPPORT"
  title="World-class support"
  ctaText="Read more about our support here"
  ctaLink="/en/support/"
  image="/media/home/support.webp"
  imageAlt="The Acme support team"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>
  Perhaps the most defining part of Acme is our support. Everyone at the company works with one ultimate goal: helping our customers. We're available every day to help you with everything from quick questions to hands-on assistance with match schedules and planning advice.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-4a6e82d1"
  eyebrow="SIMPLE PAYMENT SOLUTIONS"
  title="Accept card, Klarna or Swish payments with ease"
  ctaText="Read more about our payment solution"
  ctaLink="/en/kort-och-klarna/"
  image="/media/home/klarna_acme-3.webp"
  imageAlt="Payment with Klarna in Acme"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
  imageFocus="left center"
>
  Our modern payment solution means you can skip bank transfers entirely. Let teams pay by card or Klarna, so payments are registered automatically in the system and the money lands in your account right away.
</CmFeatureRow>

  eyebrow="ENGAGE YOUR VISITORS"
  title="Your own mobile app for Android and iPhone"
  ctaText="Get an app for your tournament"
  ctaLink="/en/app/"
  image="/media/home/usp-mobile-app.jpg"
  imageAlt="A dedicated mobile app for the tournament"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>

</CmFeatureRow>

  heading="More information for the interested"
  bg="white"
  align="left"
  contained={true}
/>

<CmColumns id="cols-8b2f47c6"
  align="left"
  columns="2"
  gap="48"
  maxWidth={1140}
>
  <CmColumn id="col-d94a10e3"
    heading="Key features"
  >
    <TextBlock id="text-6c58e2b7">
      Don't miss our other great features, including live results, live streaming, a dedicated tournament website, accommodation & catering, referees, SMS notifications and check-in.
    </TextBlock>
    <CmButton id="btn-31f7a9d0"
      label="Read more about our features"
      href="/en/missa-inte/"
      variant="green"
      icon="none"
    />
  </CmColumn>
  <CmColumn id="col-59a3e8d7"
    heading="Pricing"
  >
    <TextBlock id="text-c21f80b4">
      We keep pricing simple, with a model that works for tournaments large and small across every sport. On top of a team-based licence, there's a range of optional extra services to choose from.
    </TextBlock>
    <CmButton id="btn-e40b97c3"
      label="Read more about our pricing"
      href="/en/priser/"
      variant="green"
      icon="none"
    />
  </CmColumn>
</CmColumns>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-06c9e3b8"
  eyebrow="COLLECT PAYMENTS FOR YOUR CLUB"
  title="Acme Clubs"
  ctaText="Read more about Acme Clubs"
  ctaLink="https://clubs.acme.example/"
  image="/media/home/si.jpg"
  imageAlt="Acme Clubs"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Our sister product Acme Clubs is used by close to 1,000 clubs across Norway and Sweden to collect training fees and membership dues. It lets you tailor your collection to your needs while staying easy to use.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-f15b72a0"
  eyebrow="SPORT MATTERS IN A GLOBAL WORLD"
  title="Community, hope and growth – both at home and in East Africa."
  ctaText="Read more about the partnership"
  ctaLink="/en/lakeside-youth-cup/"
  image="/media/home/LakesideYouthCup.webp"
  imageAlt="Lakeside Youth Cup"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="light"
>
  We partner with the Lakeside Youth Cup (LYC), an annual youth festival in Tanzania that empowers young people through sport, education and community engagement.
</CmFeatureRow>

  contained={true}

  imageFocus="left center"

  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"

  eyebrow="VI ÄR STOLTA ÖVER VÅR SUPPORT"

  ctaText="Läs mer om vår support här"
  ctaLink="/sv/support/"
  image="/media/home/support.webp"
  imageAlt="Acme-supporten"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"

</CmFeatureRow>

  eyebrow="LIVESTREAMING MED GLOBEX LIVE"
  title="Sänd alla matcher live – och tjäna pengar på det"
  ctaText="Läs mer om livestreaming"
  ctaLink="/sv/streaming/"
  image="/media/streaming/pix4team-camera.gif"
  imageAlt="AI-kamera på stativ som automatiskt följer matchen"

  bgColor="light"

  eyebrow="ENGAGERA ERA BESÖKARE"

  image="/media/home/usp-mobile-app.jpg"
  imageAlt="Egen mobilapp för turneringen"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>

</CmFeatureRow>

  eyebrow="CASE STUDIE: FJORDBY BASKET FESTIVAL"

  ctaText="Läs om Fjordby Basket Festival här"
  ctaLink="/sv/fjordby-basket-festival/"
  image="/media/home/customer-story.png"
  imageAlt="Fjordby Basket Festival"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>

</CmFeatureRow>

<CmBandHeading id="band-5e17d8f0"
  heading="Mer information för den intresserade"
  bg="white"
  align="left"
  contained={true}
/>

<CmColumns id="cols-8b2f47c6"
  align="left"
  columns="2"
  gap="48"
  maxWidth={1140}
>
  <CmColumn id="col-d94a10e3"
    heading="Viktiga funktioner"
  >
    <TextBlock id="text-6c58e2b7">
      Missa inte att vi också har häftiga funktioner som livestreaming med Globex Live, liveresultat, egen hemsida för turneringen, boende & mat, domare, SMS-utskick och incheckning.

      icon="none"

  <CmColumn id="col-59a3e8d7"

    <CmButton id="btn-e40b97c3"
      label="Läs mer om våra priser"
      href="/sv/priser/"
      variant="green"
      icon="none"
    />
  </CmColumn>
</CmColumns>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-06c9e3b8"
  eyebrow="TA BETALT FÖR FÖRENINGEN"
  title="Acme Clubs"
  ctaText="Läs mer om Acme Clubs"
  ctaLink="https://clubs.acme.example/"
  image="/media/home/si.jpg"
  imageAlt="Acme Clubs"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Vår systerprodukt Acme Clubs används av uppemot 1000 klubbar för att samla in träningsavgifter och medlemsavgifter, i både Norge och Sverige. Systemet låter dig anpassa er insamling samtidigt som det är väldigt lättanvänt.
</CmFeatureRow>
